By default the command suggestion will generate a file named based on your commit. That's generally ok as long as you add the file to your commit. Someone can reorganize it later.

* ... **misspelled**, then please *correct* them instead of using the command.

See the `README.md` in each directory for more information.

:microscope: You can test your commits **without** *appending* to a PR by creating a new branch with that extra change and pushing it to your fork. The [check-spelling](https://github.com/marketplace/actions/check-spelling) action will run in response to your **push** -- it doesn't require an open pull request. https://github.com/check-spelling/check-spelling/wiki/Configuration-Examples:-patterns

https://www.regexplanet.com/advanced/perl/) yours before committing to verify it will match your lines.

  Note that patterns can't match multiline strings.

issue_context.title: Double-click word selection picks up the RPROMPT from the previous line because word wrapping is hard
issue_context.body: Discussed this with Leonard a while ago
comments: Wow it actually is! Great find

review_comments: ...but should we? If I print `a    b` and it force-wraps in the middle, shouldn't I be able to select all 4 spaces with a double click?

Eh, I didn't want to revisit too many of the decisions from the previous code.

But also, this is what prevents us from selecting **the entire text buffer** when you double-click an empty space lmao
